text: Board of Studies meeting, 18 April 2026 (CSE_AI-BOS-MOM.docx): Dr. Sandeep Palakkal proposed a skill-based course on Agentic Artificial Intelligence to familiarize students with emerging AI systems capable of autonomous decision-making, task execution and intelligent problem-solving. Resolution: approved for the 2026-27 scheme as Agentic AI (26ECAC401).
Board of Studies meeting, 18 April 2026: the 2026-27 scheme adds Cryptography & Network Security (24ECAC403) to Semester VII as part of the same revision that introduced Agentic AI.

Board of Studies meeting, 18 April 2026: Dr. Moula Hussain emphasised introducing Responsible Artificial Intelligence and Ethics in AI as a CORE course, citing fairness, accountability, transparency, privacy and responsible deployment. This was a discussion point, not a resolved core course; the curriculum currently addresses it only via an optional SWAYAM MOOC elective (24ECSE408, Responsible & Safe AI Systems).

Board of Studies meeting, 18 April 2026: student member Ms. Shruti Sutar highlighted the industry importance of web technologies and proposed separate front-end and back-end courses for more practical learning; no resolution recorded to split the existing Web Technologies Lab.

Board of Studies meeting, 18 April 2026: Mr. Vinay Kulkarni proposed an advisory committee to guide students selecting elective baskets after their second year, aligned with interests, aptitude and emerging industry requirements.

Generative AI (25ECAC307/25ECSC307) syllabus confirmed to include Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG): architecture, embeddings, vector databases and context retrieval, with a lab to build a RAG pipeline -- closing what earlier committee notes had flagged as an unverified depth gap.
Illustrative committee note (SIMULATED): Deep Learning flagged for below-target attainment on regularisation and optimisation topics; extra lab session proposed.

Illustrative committee note (SIMULATED): Cloud Computing (24ECAE317) covers Docker, Kubernetes and DevOps tooling in depth but remains elective-only; committee asked whether MLOps-specific content (model deployment and monitoring, not just general DevOps) should be added.
